svg.title: 1. Reference architecture
svg.text: Caching, search and flash sales: the reference architecture
Each layer absorbs load so the one below it never sees the spike. Most requests should end at the CDN or in Redis, never at the database.
1 Edge: answer from the closest cache, drop abuse before it costs anything
per IP, per ASN, per path
2 Gateway: decide who gets in, and what to drop first
turn off reviews, recs, live stock
3 Services: stateless, scaled out before the sale starts
4 Cache and search: the hot path, in memory
5 Async: queues turn a spike into a steady stream
6 Data: the source of truth, protected from the spike
events written in the same txn
now minus event time, alert > 30 s
Pre-warm and pre-scale at T-60 min
kill a Redis primary, fill the queue
Read path: CDN, then L1, then Redis, then a replica. Write path: reserve in Redis, queue the order, write the ledger once.
Vendor-neutral. CDN = CloudFront, Cloud CDN or Front Door. Redis = ElastiCache/Valkey, Memorystore or Azure Managed Redis. Search = OpenSearch or Elasticsearch.
